title: nfl-defensive-prop-edges-2025-2026
universal_lens: TFL as a non-sack defensive metric under run-first opponent regime; probabilistic mispricing due to conflated sack-TFL correlation. Pressure rate dynamics distinguish sack efficiency; edge pressure yields higher conversion than interior due to scheme variance.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian belief update on TFL prop mispricing using PFR and Gridiron Decoded data; conformal prediction intervals for run-first matchups. Bayesian inference maps pressure rate vs. sack rate using PFF-grade data to calibrate defensive edge value propositions.
gse_mapping: State transition model for edge rusher performance: pre-snap formation → run vs pass play → post-snap TFL generation; dynamic policy adjustment based on opponent tendencies. Situational reasoning models team rush schemes (4-man vs. blitz) to predict QB hit frequency and defensive win rate outcomes.

primitives.name: TFL Over Edge Rushers vs Run-First Opponents
primitives.verbatim_quote: # NFL Defensive Prop Edges: TFL, QB Hits, Pressures, PDs, INT Splits *Research compiled from PFF, Pro Football Reference (2025 regular season), PropsBot.AI, ESPN, Gridiron Decoded, FantasyLife, and Establish The Run.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'TFL': 'dimensionless count of tackles for loss', 'sacks': 'dimensionless count of quarterback sacks', 'run_first_offense': 'binary indicator (0/1)'}
primitives.assumptions: TFLs occur exclusively on run plays, screens, and backside pursuit; books conflate TFLs with sacks; edge rushers generate TFLs independent of pass coverage.
primitives.breakdown_regime: run-first offensive matchups where TFLs clear without sack involvement

layer2.mapping: TFL prop mispricing modeled as a conditional probability P(TFL > threshold | run_first_offense=1) ≠ P(sack > threshold | run_first_offense=1); GSE evaluates formation-specific TFL likelihood via empirical distribution.
layer2.telemetry: Observed TFL frequency vs. implied book probability in run-first contexts

primitives.name: Non-Sack TFL Disruption
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Myles Garrett** — 23.0 sacks, **33 TFL**, 39 QB hits, 60 combined tackles (Gridiron Decoded).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'sacks': 'dimensionless count', 'TFL': 'dimensionless count', 'disruption_index': 'dimensionless measure of non-sack pressure'}
primitives.assumptions: Disruption index = TFL - sacks; higher values indicate greater non-sack impact.
primitives.breakdown_regime: edge rushers with disproportionate TFL relative to sacks

layer2.mapping: Disruption index maps to a scalar field over defensive player performance space; GSI computes variance-adjusted disruption score for predictive modeling.
layer2.telemetry: Player-specific TFL minus sacks difference across game logs

primitives.name: Backside Pursuit TFL Generation
primitives.verbatim_quote: But edge rushers who excel at backside pursuit, chase down screens, and set the edge generate TFLs independently of passing situations.
primitives.assumptions: Backside pursuit generates TFLs regardless of pass context; TFLs are not dependent on pass coverage success.
primitives.breakdown_regime: post-snap defensive positioning during screen and run plays

layer2.mapping: Backside pursuit efficiency is modeled as a function of TFL generation rate; GSE simulates pursuit paths and evaluates TFL outcomes.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of TFLs generated per backside pursuit event

primitives.name: Mispriced TFL Market
primitives.verbatim_quote: PropsBot identifies this as "*the most mispriced market on his board*" because books treat it like a sack prop when it clears on run plays, screens, and pursuit.
primitives.assumptions: Market inefficiency arises from incorrect correlation between TFL and sack probabilities; empirical probability differs from book-implied.
primitives.breakdown_regime: book pricing error in TFL props vs. actual run-play TFL occurrence

layer2.mapping: Market inefficiency is defined as log( empirical_prob / book_implied_prob ); GSI uses this to compute expected value deviation in betting strategies.
layer2.telemetry: Log-ratio of empirical vs. implied TFL probabilities in run-first games

primitives.name: Interior DT Sack UNDER
primitives.verbatim_quote: **The Edge:** Interior defensive tackles with elite pressure win rates are *underpriced* on the SACK UNDER because books assume pressure = sacks.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P_w': 'Pass rush win rate (dimensionless)', 'S': 'Number of sacks (dimensionless)', 'R': 'Rate of pressure generation (per game)', 'T': 'Time (game duration)'}
primitives.assumptions: Pressure rate does not linearly correlate with sack rate; interior rushers face more structured defensive schemes limiting sack conversion.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When pressure rate exceeds sack rate by >2%, indicating inefficiency in book pricing.

layer2.mapping: Sack probability derived from pressure rate and scheme-specific conversion factors; kernel adjusts for positional and team context.
layer2.telemetry: Sack rate vs. pressure rate differential across interior DTs

primitives.name: QB Hits OVER Rusher Pressure Rate
primitives.verbatim_quote: Target **QB Hits OVER** for rushers whose pressure rate exceeds their sack rate.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'H': 'Number of QB hits (dimensionless)', 'P_r': 'Pressure rate (per game)', 'S_r': 'Sack rate (per game)'}
primitives.assumptions: QB hit frequency increases with pressure rate independent of sack rate due to sustained duress.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When P_r > S_r, indicating high-pressure environments favor hit count over sack count.

layer2.mapping: QB hit count modeled as a function of pressure rate and team scheme, mirroring sack rate behavior but with different outcome distribution.
layer2.telemetry: QB hit frequency vs. pressure rate differential

primitives.name: Team Pressure Scheme 4-Man Rush
primitives.verbatim_quote: Players on teams that generate pressure via 4-man rushes (Broncos 39.3%, Browns 38.2%) benefit because the QB is under constant duress, increasing hit opportunities even without sacks.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P_t': 'Team pressure rate (percentage)', 'H_t': 'Total QB hits per game (dimensionless)', 'S_t': 'Sacks per game (dimensionless)', 'R_s': 'Rush scheme type (categorical)'}
primitives.assumptions: 4-man rush schemes increase QB duress, leading to higher hit counts regardless of sack success.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When R_s = 4-man rush, P_t > 35% correlates with H_t > 1.5 per game.

layer2.mapping: QB hit frequency derived from team scheme type and pressure rate; kernel reflects scheme influence on hit generation.
layer2.telemetry: QB hit rate vs. team pressure rate under 4-man rush

primitives.name: Elite Pressure Win Rate Underpricing
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Key Data (2025):** - **Byron Murphy II, MIN** — 7.0 sacks, but a **9.2% pass rush win rate at DT** (17th-best among qualifiers) and **6.7% pressure rate** (9th-best).
primitives.assumptions: Book pricing fails to account for high win rate in pressure generation, leading to mispriced underdogs.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When W_r > 8% and S < 10, F_v < M_v, indicating undervaluation.

layer2.mapping: Fair value odds derived from win rate and pressure rate; mirrors market odds but adjusted for performance efficiency.
layer2.telemetry: Fair value vs. market odds for high-win-rate rushers

primitives.name: CB Tackle Base Rate
primitives.verbatim_quote: : CB Tackle Prop Base-Rate UNDER (Even High-Rate CBs Rarely Hit) **Metric:** CB tackle rate (% of snaps with a tackle/assist) vs.

primitives.assumptions: Outside CBs have limited snaps in box; run defense frequency constrains tackle accumulation.

primitives.name: Edge in Base Rate Ignorance
primitives.verbatim_quote: **The Edge:** Books price CB tackle props based on tackle rate per snap, but ignore the *base rate* — the frequency with which outside CBs reach high tackle counts.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'E': 'pricing edge from base-rate misalignment (dimensionless)', 'P_b': 'base-rate probability of high tackle game (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Market pricing ignores empirical base-rate skew; models assume uniform tackle distribution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Mispricing occurs when tackle rate is high but base rate is low.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphism between market pricing and true tackle-game probability via base-rate correction.
layer2.telemetry: Discrepancy between model-implied and actual high-tackle game frequency.

primitives.name: Limited Snap Constraint

primitives.breakdown_regime: High tackle rate under constraint of low snap exposure leads to low high-line frequency.
